To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CRISPR-CAs9 mediated knock-in of fluorescent protein tags is an effective way of labelling proteins in live cells for single molecule imaging; (2) the design of inserts is important to achieve optimal expression and protein function; (3) the expression and function of endogenously labelled proteins can be used to accurately quantify the number of receptors in a cell.
CRISPR-CAS9 mediated knock-in can improve single molecule imaging and quantification.

CRISPR-mediated insertion of fluorescent proteins into a gene locus is a useful tool for studying protein function, that there are many parameters to consider when using CRISPR-mediated knock-ins, that the choice of insert can have a large effect on protein function, and that the use of a CRISPR-mediated approach can improve the quantification of proteins in cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimisation of CRISPR-mediated knock-in for single molecule imaging and quantification, with the aim that this work will inform the development of future CRISPR-Palms.
the development of CRIPSR-PALM, and the optimisation of this approach for the study of GPCRs.
the development of CRISP-R mediated labelling of endogenous proteins and the use of this approach for the quantitative analysis of protein function.
